rounds.text: Modis Navnirman Ltd carries critical valuation and cash flow vulnerabilities that the headline multiples conceal [E29]. Despite reporting profits, the company generated negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -2 Cr in March 2026, translating to a concerning cash conversion ratio of -0.07x [E29, E30, E31]. Furthermore, insider conviction is declining as promoter shareholding dropped by 7.24 percentage points over the last three years to 63.79% in September 2026 [E36, E56]. Debt levels are also creeping upward, with borrowings rising from Rs 4 Cr to Rs 6 Cr by March 2026 [E34]. Operational risks are compounded by external hurdles, including a government-imposed stay on the Rashmi Govind Dalvi project and a pullback in foreign real estate investment inflows down to 13% in Q1 2026 [E80, E81]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 24.5x with a 36.0% margin of safety to a DCF value of Rs 601, and institutional money flow is positive [E1, E39, E40, E41].
